1.explanation:
• gather/gatherers/trace-elements-test.js: tests how the trace is captured via DevTools Protocol. This gatherer is responsible for starting/stopping the trace recording and will be the first place traces can fail to be collected when the tab is backgrounded.
• computed/trace-of-tab-test.js: processes the raw trace into a structured artifact. If no valid trace events (including FCP) are found, it throws the NO_FCP error, so this is where the absent trace becomes fatal.
• computed/metrics/first-contentful-paint-test.js: implements the FCP metric calculation and error handling for missing FCP. It’s where NO_FCP is surfaced for the Performance category.
• runner-test.js: covers the runner orchestration of gatherers and computed artifacts. It shows how errors bubble up through the lifecycle.
• index-test.js: verifies the overall entry point behavior (including extension vs. CLI differences). It can shed light on how a background tab run might diverge.
• network-records-to-devtools-log.js: needed by the extension path to convert recorded network logs into DevTools Protocol events. Any break here could starve the trace-of-tab of necessary events.
1.bug_scenario: When running the Lighthouse Chrome extension on a page that’s loaded in a background tab, the performance audit fails entirely. In the screenshot provided, all performance metrics—First Contentful Paint, Speed Index, Time to Interactive, etc.—show “Error!” and the top of the panel displays the alert “Something went wrong with recording the trace over your page load. Please run Lighthouse again. (NO_FCP)”. In other words, no trace events are recorded (so FCP can’t be found) when the tab is not active, and the extension surfaces a NO_FCP error.
